boundary-state-null's edge_only and frequency-novelty-null's primary both already pass edge/hapax/order cleanly -- those are not being re-tested as free variables here
mechanistic hypothesis, not yet tested: a unigram-frequency rule controls single-character statistics by construction but not which character PAIRS get created, which is exactly what H2 measures
not_done_before_registration: No bigram-conditional novelty stream generated or scored
No parameter selected from any transformed outcome

nu calibration (if needed) will be done as a self-consistency-only pilot targeting the same [0.65,0.75] hapax band used for frequency-novelty-null, never compared to Voynich's actual joint profile at calibration time

claim: Replacing frequency-novelty-null's unigram-frequency substitution rule with a bigram-conditional substitution rule (drawn from the replicate's own running order-1 atom-transition distribution, never Voynich) closes the H2 gap that unigram-frequency-weighting left open, passing all six frozen criteria in at least 16 of 20 primary replicates.
base_mechanism: identical to frequency-novelty-null and boundary-state-null: Naibbe cipher (voynich-units commit 956a7c4fc39981f4d116fa3f4edfccce6d065571) + identical boundary-coupling rule (beta=0.50 fixed, unchanged, not re-tested). Only the novelty-injection rule's replacement-atom distribution changes again.

representation.roundtrip_required: collapse(expand(atom)) == atom for every atomic_alphabet symbol

boundary_coupling.note: unchanged from boundary-state-null and frequency-novelty-null; not re-tested

bigram_novelty_injection.eligibility: candidate already emitted and atomic length at least 2
bigram_novelty_injection.replacement_distribution: empirical order-1 (bigram) transition frequency P(next_atom | preceding_atom_in_this_candidate), estimated from a running bigram count table over the replicate's own output emitted so far (never Voynich, never the input plaintext). preceding_atom is the candidate's OWN character at position (substitution_position - 1), fixed by the candidate itself, not by the output stream.
bigram_novelty_injection.sparse_context_fallback: if the running bigram count for the specific preceding_atom context has fewer than 20 total observations so far, fall back to frequency-novelty-null's unigram-frequency ordering for that substitution event instead of the bigram-conditional ordering (avoids acting on a near-empty conditional distribution)
bigram_novelty_injection.mutation: exhaustive search, identical structure to frequency-novelty-null: iterate every non-initial position in a random-but-seeded order; at each position, iterate all 25 alternative atoms in descending bigram-conditional-frequency order (or unigram-frequency order under the sparse-context fallback), ties broken by seeded RNG; accept the first unseen type found. Guarantees an unseen variant is found whenever one exists, matching both prior designs' search guarantee, so any difference in outcome vs. frequency-novelty-null is attributable to which statistic (unigram vs. bigram) orders the search, not how hard the search tries.
bigram_novelty_injection.cold_start: before 5 tokens have been emitted, use frequency-novelty-null's unigram-frequency order (which itself falls back to the original design's fixed cyclic order before 5 tokens) -- i.e., cold-start behavior is inherited unchanged from the prior design, only the steady-state behavior changes
bigram_novelty_injection.fallback: retain the boundary-coupled candidate unmutated if no unseen variant exists across the full search -- same condition as both prior designs

baseline.note: identical to boundary-state-null's baseline; not rerun, reused by reference (seed-invariant by construction)

edge_only.note: identical to boundary-state-null's edge_only; not rerun, reused by reference (frozen commitment, same as frequency-novelty-null's reuse)

configurations.pilot_calibration_rule: nu chosen by a self-consistency-only pilot (3 seeds, bigram_novelty_only config, beta=0) targeting hapax_share_of_types in [0.65, 0.75]. Pilot swept nu in {0.1, 0.15, 0.2, 0.25, 0.3}: 0.1 undershoots (57.9%), 0.15 undershoots (63.5%, just below floor), 0.2 lands in-band (67.4%), 0.25/0.3 also in-band (70.3%/73.0%). Frozen: nu=0.2, matching frequency-novelty-null's chosen nu exactly for a clean apples-to-apples comparison. H2 was recorded during the pilot for later interpretation but was NOT used to select nu (calibration is hapax-only, per this rule). Full pilot log in logs/2026-09-21-claude-bigram-novelty-selfreview.md.

boundary.note: reused from boundary-state-null's edge_only vs baseline comparison, not recomputed -- coupling rule is byte-identical and unchanged across all three designs

h2_recovery_diagnostic.not_a_manipulation_check: reported for interpretation only, not used in the PASS/FAIL/INVALID verdict rule
h2_recovery_diagnostic.compares: primary configuration's mean H2 against frequency-novelty-null's primary (2.946) and boundary-state-null's uniform-substitution primary (3.354), to quantify whether bigram-conditioning further reduces H2 damage relative to unigram-frequency-weighting

primary_verdict.pass: Both manipulation checks succeed and at least 16 of 20 primary replicates pass all six criteria
primary_verdict.fail: Both manipulation checks succeed and fewer than 16 of 20 primary replicates pass all six criteria
